notes: readPayload's switch (line 1142-1203) is exhaustive over NBTTag's 13 raw values (0-12); .end (0) only appears as the compound-terminator sentinel consumed by readPayload's own .compound case (line 1176-1178, `guard rawType != NBTTag.end.rawValue else { break }`) and is never itself dispatched through readPayload's switch as a value to produce -- so this fixture exercises the 12 tags that ARE returned as NBTValue cases. Also pins two int-width quirks worth preserving in the Rust port: float is read as raw 4 bytes reinterpreted via Float(bitPattern:) (line 1155) and double via Double(bitPattern:) (line 1157), not decoded as text, and list (line 1163-1173) reads its element type ONCE then reads `count` payloads of that single type -- a heterogeneous list is not representable and was never attempted here.
